This project examines the liminality of intercity night transport and the interstitial spaces that bind domestic routines to public infrastructures. Through nocturnal tram routes, overnight buses and night trains, the work documents domestic nocturnes and shared economies that unfold between platforms and sleeping berths. Methodologically, the project combines participant observation with sequential frames and archival juxtaposition. Extended stays of two to four weeks in each city enable slow, granular listening and placement within local circuits; repeated rides and early-morning returns generate visual sequences that map temporal overlap and spatial compression. Photographs will be composed with an emphasis on low-light techniques and tactile detail: careful control of aperture and ISO to preserve texture without erasing night’s subtle tonalities. Field notes, short interviews and select archival materials will be woven into captions and a printed sequence to provide contextual counterpoint.

The anticipated outcome is a photo-story fashioned for both printed folio and gallery installation, one that holds the uneasy beauty of threshold spaces while foregrounding questions of access, labor and nocturnal economies. The work seeks to make visible how cities move, sleep and sustain themselves through networks that operate after daylight’s ordinances have ended.
